title: simulacr
text: simulacr implements outbreak simulation using branching processes. main features package include: simulate_outbreak: main function, allowing simulate outbreaks specified values reproduction number, incubation period, duration infectiousness, optionally reporting delays; outputs linelist stored data.frame class outbreak, including information transmission chains; output can converted epicontacts objects visualisation, plotted using plot(...) as_epicontacts: function convert outbreak object epicontact; called implicitely plotting outbreak objects make_disc_gamma: wrapper function build discretised Gamma distributions easily draw_labels: wrapper function generate random alphanumeric labels

title: simulacr
text: brief example illustrates can simulate outbreak, different ways specifying input distributions.

title: simulacr
text: Distributions can specified different ways: discretised distribution stored distcrete object, e.g. generated via make_disc_gamma function single argument (delay) computing probability mass function (pmf) different delays vector nn positive numbers, taken pmf delays 0:(nn-1) illustrate different options , : flat distribution incubation time 1-4 days (values null probability) infectious period defined discretised Gamma distribution stored distcrete object reporting delay following Poisson distribution, specified function
code: library("simulacr")  incubation <- c(0, 1, 1, 1, 1) # numbers = unscaled PMF infectious_period <- make_disc_gamma(10, 7) # distcrete object reporting <- function(x) dpois(x, 5) # PMF function

title: simulacr
code: set.seed(1) x <- simulate_outbreak(R = runif(100, 1, 3), # random values on [1;3]                        dist_incubation= incubation,                        dist_infectious_period = infectious_period,                        dist_reporting = reporting)

what: Simulate outbreaks with transmission trees — simulate_outbreak
title: Simulate outbreaks with transmission trees — simulate_outbreak
text: function implements individual-based outbreak simulator generates transmission trees. Poisson branching process used generate new cases time, using distribution reproduction number (R) duration infectious period determine rates infection. density-dependence term used individual infectiousness decreases proportion susceptible individuals population (see details). simulated case, simulator generates individual reproduction number, date infection, symptom onset, reporting using user-specified distributions. Distributions can provided either distcrete objects, functions computing probability mass functions (PMF), vectors numbers taken PMF values 0, 1, ..., length(input) - 1

title: Simulate outbreaks with transmission trees — simulate_outbreak

text: force infection (FOI) individual \(\) \(j\) time \(t\) defined : \(\lambda_{t, \rightarrow j} = I_{t,} C_{t, \rightarrow j} \tau_{t,} w(t - T_i)\) total FOI experienced individual  time  summed possible sources infection: \(\lambda_{t, \bullet \rightarrow j} = S_{t,j} \sum_i \lambda_{t, \rightarrow j} \) follows individual \(j\) becomes infected time \(t+1\) according Bernoulli distribution probability: \( 1 - e^{-\lambda_{t, \bullet \rightarrow j}} \) keep track chains transmission, infector \(j\), denoted \(alpha_j\), drawn Multinomial distribution weighted respective FOIs directed towards \(j\): \( \alpha_j \sim \mathcal{M}(1, \lambda_{t, 1 \rightarrow j} / \lambda_{t, \bullet \rightarrow j} ,\lambda_{t, 2 \rightarrow j} / \lambda_{t, \bullet \rightarrow j} , \ldots , \lambda_{t, N \rightarrow j} / \lambda_{t, \bullet \rightarrow j}  ) \)
